what: From 01223, judged by usefulness (rule 5). Two hir-def mbe tests have failed since round 2: macro_expansion_tests::mbe::regression::test_vec, where `vec![a.]` reports "no rules expected `a`" and blames a valid token (the problem is the missing name after `.`), and mbe::matching::test_expand_bad_literal, where `m!(&k")` with ($i:literal) reports "unexpected end of macro invocation" where the first wrong token is `&`. Cause: the BestFailure tracker (failure.rs) records a fragment-parse failure at the fragment's start (track.bump only after the black-box parse succeeds), or at the end of the input. Wanted: when a fragment parser fails, the error points at the token where the parse stopped and says what the fragment expected (an expression, a literal). Then set the two expectations to that useful text, not to rustc's.
